text:
alice: Triggering hotfix deploy for release/2026.3.1 -> prod. Issue: eu-west1 embeddings OOM on specific tokenization path. Deploy bot created canary at 5% (eu-west1) with rollback on error. Need expedited approvals from @bob @emily. Patch is minimal (kv-cache bounds fix). Link: https://redwood.internal/releases/2026.3.1

bob: acked with quick review, patch LGTM. :thumbsup:

emily: setting SLA waiver for 30m window. agree to expedite. :+1:

frida: oncall is paged, pulling logs now. saw spike at 09:22 UTC. confirm regression in v2026.3.0 -> v2026.3.1 likely

deploy-bot: Canary started: 12 instances in eu-west1 (5%). Health checks green. Telemetry: errors down 0 -> 0.2% initially.

dan: If canary stays green for 10m we can roll to 50%. I want rollback criteria set: >=1% error or latency 2x baseline for 3 minutes -> automatic rollback

alice: added rollback criteria and canary timer to deploy settings.

oncall: I'm hands-on, ready to approve to accelerate. Will watch logs and be ready to trigger manual rollback if needed.

bob: approving expedite. deploybot please mark as expedited and lift normal 60m hold.

deploy-bot: Expedited approval recorded by bob and emily. Canary timer shortened to 10m. Next step: roll to 50% in 10m if stable.

frida: note for release notes: describe as 'hotfix: fix kv-cache bounds causing OOM in tokenizer; rolled canary 5% eu-west1; expedited approvals'

alice: publishing short notes and notifying customers in EU if we need to increase risk window. pushing roll now if canary remains green.

deploy-bot: Canary stable at 10m. Rolling to 50% (eu + us fallback routing excluded). Monitoring.

frida: Observability: tokenization latency unchanged, errors at 0.08% — acceptable.

oncall: confirming green. give me 5 more minutes then full roll.

alice: agreed. scheduling full roll at T+15m unless any regression.

deploy-bot: Full rollout 100% started. Rollout complete. No automatic rollback triggered.

bob: thanks everyone. filing post-release note and tag stakeholder channel.

alice: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
